segments.note: The naming obligation retains both object patterns and type-driven verb choice; given supplies the produce/consume WHAT-to-HOW context.

activation.note: Activation targets deriving or reviewing feature names from produce/consume artifacts, not implementation identifiers or artifact naming itself. Keyword and file facts are explicitly non-gating signals; diff observation is marked as requiring a new observer and semantic classification as LLM-judged rather than mechanically observable.

audit.summary: All 62 segments survive at the claimed destinations. The coder receives the naming decision, all four non-exhaustive verb families and the lessons of unusual examples, while literal application examples and provenance remain in verifier/audit material; no shared nodes or waivers are introduced.

segmentChecks.note: The then clause preserves both naming patterns and type-driven verb selection; given supplies the produce/consume WHAT-to-HOW context, and prefer[0] retains all four artifact families.
The whole-domain versus specific-resource distinction, including both patterns and rationales, is explicit in then and repeated in verifier_detail[0].
Past-tense event artifacts and all five typical verbs survive in prefer[0]; verifier_detail also makes the list non-exhaustive.
Adjective state artifacts and track, monitor, maintain, and update are retained verbatim in prefer[0] and verifier_detail[3].
The literal timebank example remains in verifier_detail[3], while prefer[2] correctly extracts the lesson that the domain need not be the colon prefix.
The literal make-choice example and its nested-name domain/resource decomposition remain in verifier_detail[1] and verifier_detail[4]; the reusable parsing caution is planner-facing.
The identify-player example remains in verifier_detail[4], and prefer[1] preserves its decision-relevant lesson that a suitable artifact-derived verb may be outside the typical list.

risks: If a feature produces or consumes several artifacts of different types or foci, the rewrite gives no precedence rule for selecting which artifact should supply the feature name; the source is likewise silent.

unobservable: change: feature name added, feature renamed, or produce/consume artifact added requires the declared diff-level observer.
finding: artifact type classification, domain/resource decomposition and focus, and verb fit are semantic LLM judgments, not Datalog-observable facts.
The given produces/consumes relationship and the when intent to derive or review a name also require task/context semantics beyond the declared keyword and file-kind signals.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the naming decision, all non-exhaustive verb families, and the lessons and literals of the unusual examples, so I agree with the auditor's PASS. A weak planner can apply the normal single-artifact rule directly, although multi-artifact precedence remains unspecified. Activation is honestly marked as partly dependent on a new diff observer and semantic judgment rather than fully deterministic.
